title: Developer Onramp Snippets and Rate Structures
summary: Working draft: short, copy-ready lines and rationale for a developer-first hosted API onramp. Includes three quickstart angles, two price-framing approaches, and a brief competitive note to inform messaging experiments.
content:
Goal: Craft short signals that make an engineer pick Redwood Hosted API for early integration — low friction, predictable spend for prototypes, clear upgrade path to Dedicated/Private.

Primary developer value props (short lines for CTAs / hero panels / banners):
- "Start building in minutes: single SDK, examples for Node/Python, no infra required."
- "Predictable performance from day one: latency profiles per model so devs can choose tradeoffs up front."
- "Cost controls that don’t slow you down: per-request caps, usage budgets, and a path to reserved capacity when you need it."

Micro-quickstarts (snackable onboarding copy + dev intent):
1) Hello-API (fast feedback loop)
   - Purpose: get a prototype generating sensible output in <10 min.
   - Steps copy: "Install SDK → paste sample prompt → stream response"
   - Signal: default model and token budget for playground; button: "Try in 10 minutes"

2) Embed-and-Search (product surface test)
   - Purpose: show embeddings + vector search in 20–30 min.
   - Steps copy: "Index 100 rows from CSV → run similarity query → compare latency"
   - Signal: include cost estimate for 10k queries/day at typical model sizes

3) Production-Preview (reliability framing)
   - Purpose: demonstrate how a single API route migrates to Dedicated behind the scenes.
   - Steps copy: "Create route → test traffic routing → preview latency SLOs"
   - Signal: mention fallback policies and basic SLA available with convertible credits

Pricing-language drafts (tone: transparent, engineer-friendly, avoid complex legalese):
A) Usage-first baseline (recommended for self-serve):
   - Headline: "Pay for what you use — clear per-token rates, no surprise bills."
   - Explainer: "Per-token pricing for generation and embeddings. Billable units shown in console and SDK client. Free tier credits for experimenting; alerts and soft-quotas by default."
   - Developer callout: "Estimate your prototype cost with our in-console estimator."

B) Predictable-step (for teams moving to the right cost/latency path):
   - Headline: "From prototype to predictable throughput — reserved capacity when you need it."
   - Explainer: "Reserve GPU-backed capacity to guarantee throughput and lower unit costs. Convert usage into a committed plan with a single click; tooling suggests a fit based on historic traffic."
   - Migration copy: "Start on pay-as-you-go. When usage stabilizes, we'll suggest a reserve that matches your 95th percentile traffic."

Competitive notes (quick scan vs three archetypes):
- Free-for-all consumer LLM APIs (fast & cheap for experiments): they win demos and low-cost sampling. Our approach: beat them on predictable latency and dev ergonomics for teams that expect to scale quickly.
- Cloud provider managed endpoints (broad infra integration): they win on enterprise contracts and ecosystem. Our approach: one-line SDK + transparent model profiles makes developer adoption easier and avoids cloud lock-in for model serving.
- Self-hosted inference stacks (control & price at scale): they win for extreme customization/cost. Our approach: provide a migration story — start hosted, export config + model pins, and move to Private with audit logs intact.

Messaging experiments to run (A/B ideas):
- A/B 1: "Start in minutes" (time-to-first-response) vs "Predictable latency" (SLO promise) on landing page — measure signup->first-API-call time and trial-to-paid conversion.
- A/B 2: Cost framing: show an "estimator" vs show "conservative cost bracket" — measure friction for teams with small budgets.
- A/B 3: Quickstarts: single unified quickstart (all-in-one) vs curated vertical quickstarts (search, chat, summarization) — measure engagement by vertical.

Copy snippets for docs/SDK readme (single-line hooks):
- "Redwood Inference hosted API — same API from prototype to production."
- "Pick a model, pick a latency profile, get a clear cost estimate before you call."
- "Streaming, function-calls, and structured outputs out of the box — no infra glue required."

Open questions / risks to resolve in follow-ups:
- What concrete free-credit sizing reduces churn while providing meaningful signal? (e.g., $50 vs $150)
- How to quantify the latency SLO on the PRD without promising enterprise SLA levels for self-serve?
- Which reserved plan minimums make sense for mid-market (GPU count, baseline RPS)?

Action items:
- Product: add a console estimator endpoint that returns cost bands for selected quickstarts (owner: Marco). Target: 2025-03-15.
- Growth: implement A/B 1 test in next landing page iteration, 4-week sprint (owner: Samira).
- Docs/SDK: create one-click repo template for Hello-API and Embed-and-Search (owner: Devon).

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Avoid complex percent-off talk in public docs; show absolute per-token $ numbers and a clear example (e.g., "a 2k-token generate ≈ $0.02 with model X").
- Keep upgrade language frictionless: "convert to reserved in console" > "contact sales" for early-stage teams.

Reference snippets and inspiration:
- Quickstarts should match common OSS dev flows (npm/pip install example first).
- Console UI should surface "estimated monthly cost" using common usage patterns (messaging app, search, summarization).

End of draft.

(Informal / working doc — will clean into separate UX copy file for landing, console microcopy, and pricing page.)
